title: Special Topics in Journalism; Media and Human Rights in the Internet Age
description: Human rights are the issues of our time, from Moscow's attack against Kyiv's imperfect democracy, from Beijing's sophisticated censorship of the internet to fierce battles over election laws and LGBTQ+ rights in the United States. The course focuses on new approaches and new roadblocks to coverage of such issues, as journalists and repressive governments refine their strategies to either obtain or suppress information about abuses. We will trace the evolution of the media's role in documenting human rights violations, from the U.S. Civil Rights movement to the Arab Spring to contemporary events online and on the ground. Students have opportunities to write each week on human rights issues and internet freedom, and to report and write in-depth, publishable articles.
